Subject: Question on operator licenses / platform fee for VPC pilot

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the throughput and the KV caching examples. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of clarifying items before we draft a PO:  

1) Operator license counts — we run two SREs and one platform engineer in the pilot. If we buy 3 operator licenses, can we schedule short-term bursts above that without pre-purchasing nodes? How are burst tokens charged versus the platform fee?

2) Usage floor vs platform fee — your commercial doc references a platform fee that amortizes the runtime and observability. For our finance team it helps to see 1) an annualized invoice example with platform fee amortized and 2) an example invoice that shows operator licenses as separate line items (monthly/annual).

3) Support tiers — does the Starter SRE tier require a separate retainer? In the RFP we listed response-time requirements (4 hour P1). Can your Starter or Business tier meet that?

I attached our RFP excerpt for the pilot for context (HealthVector_RFP.pdf). Can you send back a short spreadsheet with 2-3 pricing scenarios (pilot: 3k calls/day, scaled pilot: 20k calls/day, runway: 200k calls/day) and sample invoice lines? Ideally we can get this to Procurement by Tuesday.

Best,
Anna

Hi Anna,

Thanks — great questions. I put together three concise scenarios and a short explainer; please see the attached license_matrix_v2.xlsx and a one-pager (SOW_template.pdf) for how we typically lay out invoice lines. Quick summary below:  

Overview (short):
- Platform fee: fixed annual fee that covers control plane, telemetry retention (90 days by default), and our private deployment management tools. It is typically amortized monthly on the invoice.
- Operator licenses: per-seat/operator license for on-prem management consoles and on-call access. These are invoiced separately and not amortized into the platform fee.
- Burst capacity: available for all Dedicated/VPC customers via ephemeral node hours. Bursts are charged at an hourly burst rate; we can pre-buy burst credits at a discount if you want price predictability.

Pilot pricing scenarios (summary):
1) Small pilot (3k calls/day): low platform fee tier, 3 operator licenses, minimal burst credit (100 node-hours) — monthly estimate: platform fee amortized: $6,250; operator licenses: $1,200; token consumption: ~$800.
2) Scaled pilot (20k calls/day): mid platform fee, 5 operator licenses, burst credit (500 node-hours) — monthly estimate: platform fee amortized: $12,500; operator licenses: $2,000; token consumption: ~$5,000.
3) Runway (200k calls/day): high platform fee, 10 operator licenses, larger burst pool (5,000 node-hours) — monthly estimate: platform fee amortized: $45,000; operator licenses: $4,000; token consumption: ~$42,000.

Notes on amortization vs capex: if you prefer CAPEX treatment for platform fees, we can offer annual prepay with a discount and provide an invoice schedule that allows you to capitalize.

Support tier: our Business tier supports 4-hour P1 on-call with a 24x7 on-call SRE rota; that is a separate retainer (example values in the spreadsheet). Starter tier supports next-business-day P1 during weekdays.

Next steps: 1) I attached the spreadsheet for specific line items (license_matrix_v2.xlsx). 2) Can we book a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk Procurement through the three scenarios? I can get Marissa on the call to confirm SOW wording and invoicing cadence.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions (Mid-Market)
Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick note on SRE scope and response-time SLAs for the pilot. Internal context for pricing:

- Business support retainer covers 24x7 P1 with a 4-hour response SLA. That retainer is priced monthly and is independent of operator license counts.
- Operator licenses are for access and operations; they do not imply on-call coverage. If HealthVector wants on-call handoff to Redwood SREs, we include a managed-oncall add-on with a per-shift rate.
- For pilot acceptance, recommend a 90-day SLO ramp where we offer two P1s handled by Redwood before stepping down to HealthVector-managed on-call. That reduces initial retainer cost and gives your team time to validate runbooks.

I attached an example SOW snippet and an internal note on on-call shift pricing. Logan — if you want, I can redact the internal cost table and send a client-facing schedule.
